:::{#def-cov}
#### Covariance

For any two random variables $X, Y$:

$$\Cov{X,Y} \eqdef \E{(X - \E X)(Y - \E Y)}$$

:::

:::{#thm-alt-cov}
#### Alternative formula for covariance

$$\Cov{X,Y}= \E{XY} - \E{X} \E{Y}$$

:::

::: proof

By linearity of expectation, analogous to @thm-variance's proof:

$$
\ba
\Cov{X,Y}
&\eqdef \E{(X-\E{X})(Y-\E{Y})} && \text{(definition of covariance)} \\
&= \E{XY - X\E{Y} - Y\E{X} + \E{X}\E{Y}} && \text{(expand the product)} \\
&= \E{XY} - \E{X}\E{Y} - \E{Y}\E{X} + \E{X}\E{Y} && \text{(linearity of expectation)} \\
&= \E{XY} - \E{X}\E{Y} && \text{(algebraic simplification)}
\ea
$$

:::

:::{#lem-cov-xx}
#### The covariance of a variable with itself is its variance

For any random variable $X$:

$$\Cov{X,X} = \Var{X}$$

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\Cov{X,X}
&= \E{XX} - \E{X}\E{X}
&& \text{(@thm-alt-cov)}
\\&= \E{X^2} - \sqf{\E{X}}
\\&= \Var{X}
&& \text{(@thm-variance)}
\ea
$$

:::

:::{#cor-var-lincom2}
#### Variance of a sum of two random variables

For any two random variables $X$ and $Y$ and scalars $a$ and $b$:

$$\Var{aX + bY} = a^2 \Var{X} + b^2 \Var{Y} + 2(a \cd b) \Cov{X,Y}$$

:::

::: notes

The proof is a direct expansion of @def-variance and @def-cov,
analogous to the two-line proof of @lem-cov-xx above;
we omit it here since this page's role is to state the result
we later depend on, and leave its derivation as a review exercise.

:::

::: notes

This corollary is why two variables' covariance matters for combining them:
if $X$ and $Y$ are [independent](#def-indpt), $\Cov{X,Y}=0$
and the variance of their sum is just the sum of their variances.
See rme's
[Probability chapter](https://morrison-lab.github.io/rme/probability.html#thm-var-lincom)
for the general $n$-variable version and the vector/matrix forms of
variance and covariance.

:::
